geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the lift-only cap into a courtyard/public-void macro so the dominant body can answer the street edge with a legible ground figure while preserving the protected ancestry.
Carve a usable open space rather than a decorative subtraction.
Align the opening with the program-frame access side so the ground response is visibly tied to the verified frontage logic.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the generic lift-only finish with a more program-legible sectional operator that can create an active ground response and a clearer public void.
Reduce the dominant uplift so the mass sits more firmly on the ground and can read as a compact neighborhood building rather than a floating bar.
Strengthen the ground contact so the lifted portion reads as a deliberate public threshold rather than incidental thin supports.
Swap the repeated split artifact for a courtyard-producing macro that can generate a legible void tied to the site edge.
Keep the dominant bar axis while making the split operate across the width of the mass rather than fragmenting the long edge.
Ensure the void remains open enough to be read as public space rather than a nearly closed slit.

rationale: The candidate reads as a long rectangular bar with a small clipped end and minor split artifacts, but not as one coherent neighborhood-living massing idea across all views. It is broadly stable in silhouette and unlikely to be a broken repair, yet the form is too box-like and too weakly articulated at the ground to satisfy the brief. The thick blue access edge is not answered by a legible public void, court, or entry seam; instead the mass remains largely sealed/semantically indifferent to frontage. The top view shows a mostly generic bar within the parcel rather than a strong parcel-driven open-space figure. The program can plausibly be housed in a compact bar, but the visible section does not yet express the required active threshold and public terrace logic, so program_fit_hard_pass fails.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus/community-center than compact street building; if copied too literally it may over-spread the footprint and weaken the required street threshold.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise, winged composition organized around a clear shared void and terrace-like circulation can support neighborhood living while keeping the mass legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Single-story pavilion language is too light and too flat for the requested 5-floor capacity-aware massing.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple grounded pavilion with a strong entry canopy and direct street response can translate into a neighborhood commercial threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual only: the candidate is not currently achieving this kind of sectional continuity; do not copy the long terraced housing form directly.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/sectional massing can create a strong inhabited roof and communal void when the section is program-driven.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied; the failure is semantic and relational, not containment.
Visible access response is weak on the verified frontage edge.
The silhouette is coherent, but coherence is mostly one-dimensional rather than spatially rich.
Do not overvalue the stepped/terraced precedent; this candidate is not actually resolving a meaningful inhabited section.
